To understand the concept of relativity, specifically time dilation, imagine a pair of identical, highly precise hourglasses. One hourglass stays on the ground, while the other is placed inside a spaceship that travels at an incredibly high speed, close to the speed of light.

For the person inside the spaceship, everything feels completely normal. The sand in their hourglass falls at the usual rate, and they age normally. However, if someone on the ground were to look at the spaceship's hourglass through a powerful telescope, they would see the sand falling much more slowly than their own. This isn't because the hourglass is broken; it's because time itself is passing more slowly for the moving object relative to the stationary observer.

Think of it like two people walking at the same speed, but one is walking on a moving walkway at an airport. To the person on the walkway, their steps feel normal. But to someone standing still watching them, the person on the walkway covers more ground in the same amount of time. In the case of relativity, it's not just distance that changes, but the very fabric of time itself. The faster you move through space, the slower you move through time relative to someone who is stationary.
